rows.description: A wise writer produces a rough draft without judging, leaves it for a while and then edits with fresh eyes. Separating creating from editing prevents both blank-page fear and endless polishing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A busy colleague reads a rambling message, cannot tell what is needed, and either delays replying or guesses wrongly. Unclear writing shifts the work of interpretation onto the reader.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A skilled writer states the point first, uses short sentences, gives dates and numbers, and ends with the exact action needed. Reading it aloud and cutting a third usually improves it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Fear of standing before the class [Actor]
rows.description: A schoolchild reciting or presenting feels a racing heart, dry mouth and forgets the lines, sure that everyone is judging. Gentle repeated practice in low-stakes settings makes it less frightening.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager presents by reading each slide word for word, eyes on the screen, to cope with nerves. It feels safe but loses the audience, who could have read it themselves.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student before a viva or seminar believes every small stumble is noticed and remembered. Audiences usually notice far less than the speaker fears and are mostly thinking about themselves.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: An audience member notices a speaker's shaking voice and often feels sympathy, not judgment. A small kind gesture such as attentive nodding helps the speaker recover.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, interest, empathy

rows.description: A listener sees a presenter dump many details with no clear message and stops following. People remember one or two clear points and the way a talk made sense, not the volume of content.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A confident presenter knows the main message, rehearses aloud, keeps slides light and invites questions, saying honestly when something is unknown. Preparation and honesty steady the nerves better than pretending.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child explaining a game or homework to a younger sibling mixes real help with bossiness and impatience. Explaining forces the older child to organise their own understanding, even when the teaching is clumsy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
